title: One Soup Dumpling, 18 Folds, and Hidden Molten Broth | China Travel Expert
description:
One soup dumpling, 18 folds on top, and a mouthful of hidden broth.

Shanghai's xiaolongbao (小笼包) is the original soup dumpling — and the soup isn't poured in. The filling is mixed with a savory aspic that sets like jelly, then melts back into hot broth as the dumpling steams. The wrapper is pleated by hand: Din Tai Fung's benchmark is exactly 18 folds on every one. The dish was refined in Nanxiang — now part of Shanghai's Jiading district — back in the 1870s.

🧭 Expert Tip: Never bite a xiaolongbao whole. Nip a small hole in the side, sip the scalding soup out first, then dip the rest in black vinegar with ginger — that's how locals eat it without burning their mouth.

小笼包：18 个褶，汤在里面——先咬个小口把汤吸掉，别烫着。
